entries.title: Proverbs 13:2
segments:
CHAP. XIII. 
 
  V. 2. Shall eat-Shall receive comfort, and benefit by his wise and profitable discourses.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:6
segments: V. 6. Keepeth him-From that over-throw which befal sinners.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:7
segments: V. 7. Maketh rich-Some men who have little or nothing, pretend to have great riches.  Maketh rich-Some rich men profess to be poor.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:8
segments: V. 8. Riches-Riches enable a man to redeem his life when it is in greatest danger, and poverty preserves a man from many injuries.  Because they are cautious, that they may not provoke others; and because they are esteemed objects of pity.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:9
segments: V. 9. The light-The prosperity.  Rejoiceth-Shines with a pleasant and constant brightness.  Rejoicing is here ascribed to the light, as it is to the sun,
, metaphorically. Put out-Their felicity shall have a hidden end.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:10
segments: V. 10. Pride-It is chiefly, pride which blows up the coals of contention.  Well-advised-Who are not governed by their passions, but by prudent considerations.  Wisdom-Which teaches them to avoid contention.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:12
segments: V. 12. Hope deferred-Delays in obtaining what a man passionately desires.  The desire-The good desired.  A tree of life-It is satisfactory, and reviving.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:13
segments: V. 13. The word-The word of God.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:14
segments: V. 14. The law-The instruction, or counsel; as the word law, is frequently understood in scripture.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:15
segments: V. 15. Giveth-Makes a man acceptable to God.  Rough-Offensive and hateful to God and men, as rough ways are to a traveller.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:16
segments: V. 16. Knowledge-Considerately and discreetly.  Layeth open-By his foolish actions.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:17
segments: V. 17. A messenger-Who is unfaithful in the execution of that which is committed to his charge.  Is health-Procures benefit, as to his master, so to himself.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:19
segments: V. 19. Sweet-Whatsoever men earnestly desire, the enjoyment of it is sweet to them; therefore sinners rejoice in the satisfaction of their sinful lusts, and abhor all restraint of them.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:21
segments: V. 21. Evil-Punishment proportionable to their sin.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:23
segments: V. 23. The poor-Poor persons by their diligent labours, and God's blessing often grow rich.  Destroyed-Or, consumed, brought to poverty, for want of discretion.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:24
segments: V. 24. Hateth his son-His fond affection, is as pernicious to him as hatred.
